generated_outputs.assessment: The generator preserves the audited-surface/name-collision boundary, but the manual version is more precise about which Iris-like surfaces create which risk.
The generator preserves ecosystem-surface separation and blocks roadmap/traction inference, but the manual version handles unrelated watermelon references more sharply.
The generator performs best on the stable case because the required move is restrained proof distribution rather than nuanced ambiguity handling.

what_worked: The generator preserves the same high-level candidate shape as the manual artifacts.
The generator correctly carries mode and pressure_subtype into the prose candidate.
LaunchDarkly remains light and does not invent ambiguity.
Every generated dimension includes evidence_boundary, uncertainty_retained and overreach_avoided.
Unsupported pressure subtypes abstain instead of generating.
what_is_weaker_than_manual: Dimension prose is more templated and less case-specific than the manual candidates.
The generator does not yet use relation_type details deeply enough inside each dimension.
The generator can name evidence families, but it does not yet rank which evidence is most important for a dimension.
The generator does not yet produce the sharper editorial compression seen in manual Iris and Watermelon.

safety_assessment.main_reason: The generator preserves epistemic boundaries, but its prose is still a lab candidate and lacks enough case-specific editorial judgement.
unsafe_to_do_next: remove human review from strong-mode ambiguity cases

recommendation.next_step: create a side-by-side Lab comparison artifact showing baseline, manual state-first, and generated state-first for the three cases
recommendation.rationale: The generator is structurally valid, but humans need to see whether generated prose is good enough compared with manual candidates before any deeper implementation.
